summary.title: Interview advice that got me offers from Google, Microsoft, and Stripe
summary.one_liner: Four non-obvious tactics for tech interviews: work with recruiters, practice in real low-stakes interviews, ask questions freely, and stay interview-ready even when not job hunting.
keywords: how to prepare for coding interviews
stay employable while not job hunting
takeaways: Recruiters have already screened you technically by the time they call, and they want to help you interview well; ask them what to prepare and reschedule if needed.
Real interviews, even at companies you don't care about, build pressure tolerance and teach you more than LeetCode practice.
Write down interview questions the same evening, then revisit them days later to craft better answers for behavioral and design questions.
Asking questions and admitting gaps during an interview can leave a positive impression; sincere curiosity is a good sign to interviewers.
Interview at least once a year even when employed, and check whether your tooling (such as working code in a plain online IDE) matches current interview formats.
summary.summary: The author, a former Microsoft, Google, and Stripe engineer, shares personal interview tactics that go beyond standard advice on coding practice. The post is a first-person essay with anecdotes rather than a technical tutorial. It covers four tips: use recruiters to prepare and reschedule, practice in real interviews to manage pressure and refine answers, ask questions freely during interviews, and keep interviewing skills current even when not job hunting. Each tip is backed by a story, such as a career fair interview at Bloomberg and a tech screen where the lack of IDE tooling caused the author to struggle.
